question: What percentage of people were below the poverty line in India in 2011 - 2012 as per the Economic Survey 2013 - 14, released by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**21.9%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Economic Survey 2013-14** released by the **Ministry of Finance, Government of India**, the percentage of people below the poverty line in India during the year **2011-12** was calculated to be **21.9%**.
 
• This data is based on the **Tendulkar Methodology**, which takes into account both **rural and urban poverty**.
 
• The poverty line is determined by considering the minimum income or expenditure required to meet basic needs like food, clothing, housing, and education.
 
• In terms of absolute numbers, this percentage implies that approximately **269 million people** were living below the poverty line in India in 2011-12.
 
• The **Planning Commission of India** played a crucial role in estimating poverty figures during this period.
 
• The poverty ratio was higher in **rural India** (25.7%) compared to **urban India** (13.7%) as per the same survey.
 
• Efforts by the Government of India, such as **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** and **National Food Security Act**, were aimed at alleviating poverty and improving the standard of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **10.2%__**
 __
 
• The value is significantly lower than the actual poverty rate calculated for India during 2011-12, and it does not represent the conditions accurately as per official surveys.
 
 
 
• **0.187__**
 __
 
• This appears to be a misrepresentation or incorrect format of data. It is likely not related to the percentage of people below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Additional Key Points__**
 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is an annual document released by the **Ministry of Finance** that reviews the economic development of the country over the past year.
 
• The **Tendulkar Methodology**, introduced by the **Suresh Tendulkar Committee**, marked a shift from calorie-based poverty estimation to one based on per capita consumption expenditure.
 
• India has seen a decline in poverty rates over the years due to various socio-economic reforms and government welfare schemes.
